450	the last verse of the song: "And He will cleanse His land, His people." We

451	always read this parashah between Rosh Hashanah

452	and Yom Kippur, almost always, Parashat Haazinu,

453	and the atonement

454	on Yom Kippur comes after the judgment that took place on Rosh

455	Hashanah. And even after the judgment of Rosh Hashanah, we have

456	the ten days of Teshuvah,

457	whose proper use can sweeten the judgment, can change

458	even the decree. And let us hope that this is the process that is indeed

459	felt during the days that still remain until

460	Yom Kippur, and then HaShem will atone for the sins of

461	His people and His land. True, the atonement also comes after

462	the suffering and pain that the people of Israel endured throughout the generations,

463	but we are close. Every day and every year that passes

464	brings us nearer to the time of the ultimate redemption

465	and to the time of atonement.

466	Let us conclude this Dvar Torah with a wish to all

467	the listeners and to all the people of Israel: may we all have a Shabbat

468	shalom and blessed, and good tidings, and a Yom Kippur

469	that atones for all the damage, all of it. May we all have

470	a good final sealing, a good year, and good tidings.
